page: Google Cloud Platform z4d-highmem-16-standardlssd is a storage-optimized instance tailored for workloads demanding substantial local storage capacity and memory density. The instance is built on an x86_64 architecture with 16 dedicated vCPUs and 126 GB of system memory, providing approximately 7.88 GB of RAM per core. Hardware acceleration via discrete GPUs is not present on this machine profile.

A key component of this instance configuration is the integrated local NVMe SSD storage offering 3,758 GB of direct-attached capacity. This setup prioritizes high-throughput local I/O operations and low storage latency, avoiding network-attached storage bottlenecks. Because this instance allocates dedicated CPU resources alongside a fixed local NVMe array without bundled public IPv4 addresses, its operational cost efficiency is realized primarily in scenarios where the substantial local NVMe storage and high memory footprint are consistently utilized.

The combination of 126 GB RAM, 16 dedicated vCPUs, and high-capacity NVMe SSD storage makes this virtual machine appropriate for I/O-sensitive transactional databases, distributed storage nodes, in-memory caching systems with local persistence, and analytical data processing engines.
description: Google Cloud Platform z4d-highmem-16-standardlssd is a storage-optimized virtual machine designed for I/O-intensive and data-heavy enterprise workloads. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs based on the x86_64 architecture and provides 126 GB of system memory, equating to 7.88 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage capabilities are anchored by a bundled 3,758 GB local NVMe SSD, delivering low-latency, direct-attached disk access without relying on network-attached persistent storage for scratch or working volumes. Hardware accelerators such as GPUs are not included, and complimentary public IPv4 addresses are omitted. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance maximizes value when applications systematically saturate its large local NVMe storage and high memory allocation. These technical characteristics make the instance suitable for distributed NoSQL databases, transactional relational database systems, real-time analytics, and data pipeline caching layers requiring high throughput and low-latency storage access.
